experiment: Random initialization and recovery under identifiable pairwise counts (Section 6.3 and Appendix G.7)
task: 256 bird/cat inputs with a 513-parameter head on frozen ResNet-18 features. Every query gives the number of cats in a pair of inputs. Same-class pairs identify both labels; mixed pairs form a connected degree-eight graph and leave open which input is which. rho is the weight of the mixed-pair mean loss.

random_initialization.conditions_note: identified_inputs is the number of inputs with a same-class query; the mixed-pair graph is kept in every condition, so the queries always determine every label. A null rho gives every retained query the same weight.
random_initialization.initialization: Head weights and bias independently uniform on [-1/sqrt(512), 1/sqrt(512)], without using concept labels; the heads of a training set are shared by all conditions and optimizers
random_initialization.optimizers: Full-batch gradient descent (gd), or SGD over independently sampled queries drawn with probability proportional to their weight (sgd); no momentum or weight decay
random_initialization.step_size: 1 / (1.5 max_i ||x_i||^2), the same for every condition and optimizer of a training set

neighborhood_entry.source: Every gradient-descent run of that condition that ends with every training concept wrong, continued with unchanged objective and step size
neighborhood_entry.neighborhood: The ball around the finite wrong state of Appendix F.3 in which gradient descent provably contracts toward it, with b = log 4

recovery.source: The final states of the neighborhood-entry runs
recovery.rule: Train with low_rho. At a check, restore original_rho if all observed counts are correct and the loss at original_rho is below 2 log(2) / n; original_rho is then kept
recovery.comparison: Unchanged gradient descent at original_rho from the same states and for the same number of updates
